3 years ago I wrote this piece for @theatlantic.com about why we mustn’t take public health for granted.

This is long before this admin’s deep cuts to public health.

With the massive Cyclospora outbreak, I couldn’t help thinking about my own warning from the past.

posts.text: Craig Spencer has followed every Ebola outbreak since 2014 and seen how the world’s capacity to control the virus has improved—but the U.S. is forgetting what made that possible, he argues.
posts.summary: Warns U.S. is abandoning proven Ebola control strategies

What impact will AI have on that skill?

posts.text: The milder symptoms—and maybe lower death rate—of the current Ebola outbreak are good news. But they could paradoxically make it harder to control the virus. Dr. @craigspencer.bsky.social says patients are naming fewer contacts and those unfollowed contacts “can blow up into something much bigger."
posts.summary: Warns milder symptoms could paradoxically complicate outbreak control

posts.text:
Dr. @craigspencer.bsky.social recalls surviving #ebola with Providence Journal. As someone who fought & survived it, his voice is an important one.

He shares that the current outbreak in the DRC could get far worse because of US cuts on the global health programs needed to fight it.
posts.summary: Warns global health funding cuts could worsen current Ebola outbreak

posts.text:
We continue to think that if we protect ourselves here, that's sufficient, but the only thing that's going to lower risk for Americans is making sure there is no #Ebola. — @craigspencer.bsky.social 

Protests continue in Kenya as quarantine facility being built by the US for American citizens.
